summary: Democratic Senator John Kerry announced that he will be a candidate for his party's nomination for the 2004 presidential race.
A group of Swift Boat Veterans for Truth ran a campaign questioning John Kerry's Vietnam War record, which is widely cited as a major factor in his loss to George W. Bush.

John Kerry receives the endorsement of South Carolina's only black congressman, James Clyburn, in his Democratic presidential campaign.

John Kerry is described as the undisputed frontrunner for the Democratic presidential nomination after wins in Iowa and New Hampshire, with polls showing him leading in Missouri and gaining in other upcoming primary states.

John Kerry won the Michigan and Washington Democratic caucuses, defeating his rivals and strengthening his lead for the Democratic presidential nomination.

John Kerry leads Democratic rival John Edwards by significant margins in Ohio, New York, and California ahead of Super Tuesday primaries.

John Kerry, the presumptive Democratic presidential candidate, is noted for his strong environmental voting record and campaign platform, contrasting with George Bush's environmental policies.
John Kerry criticized President George Bush over gay marriage and broken promises after winning primary victories in Utah, Idaho, and Hawaii.

John Kerry's campaign released the "Fought for America" advertisement, which highlighted his military service and policy priorities.
John Kerry secures the Democratic nomination for president, prompting intensified attacks on his anti-war activities during the Vietnam era.
John Kerry released over 130 pages of his naval military records, documenting his Vietnam War service and citations, but declined to release his medical records.

John Kerry launched a $25 million advertising campaign aimed at redefining his image after sustained attacks from the White House.

John Kerry meets with Richard Gephardt as part of the final stage of his search for a vice-presidential running mate.

Polls show John Kerry received no post-convention bounce, with George Bush leading among likely voters.

Polls show John Kerry leading in 13 of 20 battleground states and ahead in electoral college estimates, while remaining level with George Bush nationally despite attacks on his Vietnam war record.

John Kerry launched a stinging personal counter-attack against the Bush administration, singling out Vice President Dick Cheney for having "refused to serve" in Vietnam.

A Washington Post and ABC poll shows John Kerry trailing George Bush by 52-43 percentage points nationwide, with 50 days left in the presidential campaign.

Sinclair Broadcast Group plans to air a film days before the presidential election portraying John Kerry as betraying fellow soldiers in Vietnam, prompting Democrats to file a legal complaint with the Federal Election Commission.

John Kerry returned to Boston on election day, voted at the State House, and awaited the outcome of the presidential election.

John Kerry is invited to join his former band the Electras for their 45th anniversary gig in Washington next year.

Senator John Kerry promised that the US Congress would pass major climate and energy legislation if a successful deal was reached at the Copenhagen climate talks.
John Kerry is reported as one of the frontrunners to replace Hillary Clinton as Secretary of State, though no appointment has been made.
John Kerry becomes the frontrunner for secretary of state following Susan Rice's withdrawal from consideration.

Barack Obama nominated John Kerry to be secretary of state.

John Kerry begins his role as secretary of state by calling Israeli and Palestinian leaders, among other diplomatic calls.

John Kerry meets Canadian foreign minister John Baird in Washington, with the Keystone XL pipeline expected to be discussed.

John Kerry arrives in London on the first stop of his first foreign trip as US secretary of state.

US Secretary of State John Kerry flew to Geneva to rejoin weekend talks over Iran's nuclear program as negotiators appeared close to a historic deal.
John Kerry arrived in Geneva to join William Hague and other foreign ministers in negotiations on Iran's nuclear programme.
Secretary of State John Kerry played a key behind-the-scenes role in the Geneva talks that produced an interim nuclear deal with Iran, which officials said could rehabilitate his political career.

US Secretary of State John Kerry briefed President Barack Obama by video conference on developments in the Iran nuclear talks in Lausanne.
